scope: GET response headers and HTTP serializers of active Hub
method: Read-only GET capture plus static inspection of _send/_send_bytes; no POST.

findings.statement: The shared response serializer sets Content-Type, Length and no-cache but no browser hardening headers.
No CORS header was observed; same-origin default is safer than wildcard but should be explicit if APIs are proxied.
Hardening matters if HUB_HOST becomes non-loopback; current process remains loopback.

recommendations.action: Add X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and an explicit CORS policy.
Use a strict CSP appropriate to inline scripts or migrate scripts/nonces; avoid weakening for convenience.
Suppress version details in Server header and add request IDs/security audit events.
Require TLS/auth/reverse proxy before any non-loopback bind; headers do not replace access control.
